exposure: Fertility-sparing treatment (FST) for cervical cancer (non-radical surgery vs. radical trachelectomy)
Regular ultrasound cervicometry in pregnancy with subsequent prophylactic procedures
cohort: The cohort consists of 733 patients who underwent fertility-sparing treatment for cervical cancer across 44 centers in 13 countries.
finding: Patients undergoing non-radical fertility-sparing surgery had significantly higher pregnancy rates compared to radical trachelectomy, which led to a higher rate of preterm births; furthermore, regular ultrasound cervicometry with prophylactic procedures in pregnancy significantly increased the delivery of a live fetus.
